name: addressing
description: The addressing shapes an ISE ActiveList actually returns. A MAB row with a MAC and no address at all, an 802.1X row with a framed address and no calling_station_id, a row whose calling_station_id is in Cisco dotted-quad notation, and a row whose device_ip_address is 127.0.0.1. Proves the run survives a session with only one of the two correlators, that dotted MACs are normalized to colon form, and that a loopback address never reaches an interface: the loopback row still emits an asset, carried by its MAC alone. A build that put 127.0.0.1 on the interface would fail no_loopback_interfaces here. A fifth row carries NEITHER a calling_station_id NOR any address -- the shape a session logged against a network device rather than an endpoint takes. It has nothing to correlate on (audit_session_id names the SESSION, not the endpoint, and matchBehavior already excludes it from matching), so it cannot become an asset. It used to be dropped in silence; the skip is now logged, and it names the session id rather than user_name, which is a person's login.
